errors.quote: For $0\le i<f-1$ (top position set aside) write the $K$-bit segments
errors.problem: The page never goes back to the top selected position j_{f-1}. The procedure it describes (eight shifts plus correction implementing T_0) never performs y_{j_{f-1}} xor= x_{j_{f-1}}, and for f=1 it does nothing, although the opening sentence claims XORs "at all selected positions". The page also leaves T_0 undefined ("the XOR permutation T_0"). The paper defines T_0 as performing the XORs only at j_0,...,j_{f-2}, and then applies a final two-bit XOR to x_{j_{f-1}},y_{j_{f-1}} by Lemma elementary-streams in O(V). That last step is the entire algorithm when f=1.

errors.quote: Since $T_0$ and $S_0$ are bijections agreeing off $\mathcal B,$ $T_0S_0^{-1}$ fixes $\mathcal B^c$ and permutes $\mathcal B,$
errors.problem: As written, the inference does not hold: two bijections that agree off B only give that T_0S_0^{-1} fixes S_0(B^c). The paper also uses the fact that T_0 preserves the guard values and hence B, so that S_0(B^c)=T_0(B^c)=B^c.

errors.problem: Lines (2),(4),(5),(7) update z, not y. The paper says that for those lines y and z are interchanged in the formula.

errors.quote: substituting the parity pairs of $(u,w)$ shows the first four lines induce the cycle $(00\ 01\ 10)$
errors.problem: The paper's cycles act on the four corners of every square {2a,2a+1}x{2b,2b+1}, which are values, not just parity labels. Without that, the following "So (u',w')=..." (quotients preserved, w restored) does not follow from a permutation of parity pairs.
